newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS sends bills for oil royalties shortfall.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS sends bills for oil royalties shortfall.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service said Thursday it sent bills out to 10 companies for slightly more than $108 million in back royalty payments for oil extracted from federal land in California in 1983-1988.
The MMS also said it subpoenaed seven companies that did not respond to its requests for information on possible royalties underpayments.
The MMS has said it will try to collect some $440 million in underpaid royalties from California production.

The agency sent bills to Atlantic Richfield Co, Koch Oil, Marathon Oil, Mobil Corp, Oryx Energy Co, Phillips Petroleum, Shell Oil Co, Texaco, Unocal Corp, and Occidental Petroleum Corp, a spokesman said.

This was for underpayments for oil produced between October 1983 and February 1988. The MMS said detailed audits of integrated company records for that period were not required because MMS is basing the royalty value on Alaska North Slope oil rpices, which are readily available, instead of sales contract prices.
In September, the MMS sent bills to companies for post 1988 production, and sent letters to 20 companies seeking audit information.

The MMS spokesman said subpoenas have been issued to seven companies that did not comply with the request for information. He said those were Unocal, Shell, Pennzoil Co, Occidental, Mobil, Exxon Corp, and Chevron.
The agency has said it would pursue payments from 20 companies that accounted for 97 percent of the production on federal land in California.

Within a few months, the agency said it expects to issue bills to the same companies for production from January 1980-September 1983, using ANS prices as a valuation basis. But it said those orders may be more difficult because royalty calculations were not computerized at that time.
The agency said it also is pursuing similar oil valuation issues nationwide, but the spokesman said that investigation is in its early stages.
The MMS said audit personnel have been told to hold open the most recent audit period of 1989-1992 for further examination to see if crude oil payments were made properly in areas outside California.
